On this basis, a person's saying: "Glory be to Allah, and praise be to Allah, and Allah is greatest" is considered thanks; and his saying when he eats food or drinks a drink: "Praise be to Allah" (meaning for this food or drink) is also considered thanks.

As for the third, which is the limbs: it is that a person performs obedience to Allah, whether related to this blessing or not; he uses this blessing to help him in obedience, or performs an act of obedience that is not related to this blessing.

"Blessings from me have benefited you in three ways: my hand, my tongue, and the hidden heart."

("My hand"): this is the limb. ("My tongue"): this is the speech of the tongue. ("And the hidden heart"): this is the acknowledgment of the heart.

If someone says: you mentioned that thanks by the tongue is praising Allah, the Exalted, whether it relates to this blessing or to other than it; does His saying, "But as for the blessing of your Lord, proclaim it" [al-Duha 11], fall under this?

* Student: Yes, it falls under it.

* The Shaykh: Yes, this falls under it: ﴿But as for the blessing of your Lord, proclaim it﴾, so it is included in these noble verses.

If someone says: does this necessitate boasting? We say: no, this is not by way of boasting, but by way of humility before Allah, and that these blessings are from Allah, as the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "I am the master of the children of Adam on the Day of Resurrection, and I say it without boasting."[[Recorded by al-Tirmidhi (3148) from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him.]]

Then Allah the Exalted said: (﴿And﴾ mention ﴿the day He calls them, and says﴾ [al-Qasas 74]). The author, by his estimate of (mention), informed us that the adverbial phrase ﴿and the day He calls them﴾ is connected to an implied verb whose estimate is (mention).

His saying: ﴿and the day He calls them﴾, i.e., Allah, and that is the Day of Resurrection, ﴿and says: "Where are My partners whom you used to claim?"﴾ [al-Qasas 62]. Do I think this has passed us? Yes, it passed us recently, and this is a repetition of the warning against shirk; meaning: remember also the calling a second time: ﴿and the day He calls them and says: "Where are My partners whom you used to claim?"﴾ [al-Qasas 62].

The meaning of ﴿My partners﴾: those whom you made partners to Me in creation, provision and management, or in worship?

* Student: In worship.

* The Shaykh: Yes, those who associated others with Allah when the Messenger was sent, in worship; and they acknowledged that Allah alone is the Creator and Provider. But among people there are those who also deny that and say: there is no lord, or say: these things were brought into being by pure nature. This too is a kind of shirk; the first is pure suspension (ta'til mahd): whoever denies a god altogether is purely a negator (mu'attil), and the second is a polytheist.

His saying: ﴿whom you used to claim﴾: the author said: (It was mentioned a second time so that there could be built upon it: ﴿And We drew out from every nation a witness﴾ [al-Qasas 75], i.e., brought forth, ﴿and their prophet is a witness against them for what they said. ﴿And We said: Bring your proof﴾ for what you claimed of association; ﴿then they will know that the truth belongs to Allah﴾ [al-Qasas 75], i.e., lordship belongs to Allah) to the end.

We stop here (...).

* Student: (...)?

* The Shaykh: No; because it is a statement. It is one of the limbs without doubt, but it is a statement, and therefore (...).

[Real and established for Allah in a perfect manner, and not like the mercy of created beings.]

(...)

For example, if it is said: mercy implies weakness and softness and the like, we say: that is with respect to the created being; it is a real mercy that is not like the mercy of created beings.

* Among its benefits: showing Allah's blessing in the alternation of night and day: ﴿out of His mercy He made for you the night and the day﴾ [al-Qasas 73].

* Among them: that the night is for rest and the day is for seeking livelihood; by His saying: ﴿that you may rest therein﴾ at night, ﴿and that you may seek of His bounty﴾ [al-Qasas 73] in the day.

* There branches from this matter a benefit, which is what the scholars (al-Ashab), may Allah have mercy on them, mentioned concerning the division between two wives: if a man has two wives and wishes to divide between them, is the basis of division the night or the day? The basis is the night for one whose livelihood is by day, and the day for one whose livelihood is by night; if the matter is unclear to us, the basis is the night, since it is the place of rest.

* Also among the benefits of the verse: that the night is the place of rest, and rest in it is in sleep; rest is more beneficial to the body than that by day.

* Also: affirmation of causes, in His saying: ﴿and that you may seek of His bounty﴾, i.e., that you may seek. Provision does not come down from heaven merely; rather there must be seeking. If you do not take this cause by which provision is obtained, provision will not come; because Allah, the Exalted, is Wise, and has linked causes to their effects. So in the verse ﴿and that you may seek of His bounty﴾ is the affirmation of causes, and that matters come by their causes.

* Among them: that provision is a favour from Allah, mighty and majestic is He, and bounty and gift: ﴿and that you may seek of His bounty﴾ [al-Qasas 73]. It is not obtained merely by a person's exertion and striving; how many a person strives and toils and yet his provision is narrow, and how many a person does fewer means than the first and then is granted abundance in provision.

* Among the benefits of the verse: the importance of thanks, by His saying: ﴿and that perhaps you may be thankful﴾ [al-Qasas 73].

* Among them: that it is fitting for a person to have insight into what Allah has subjected to him, so that he may thank Allah for it. Allah has subjected to us the night and the day, the sun and the moon; so let us take a lesson from this by which we arrive at thanking Allah, glorified and exalted is He, for that.

* * *

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And the day He calls them and says: "Where are My partners whom you used to claim?"﴾ [al-Qasas 74].

Is it taken from its benefits what preceded in the first verse, or not?

* Student: Yes.

* The Shaykh: Has this verse not passed us in its wording? Yes, it passed us in its wording, so its benefits are referred to what preceded.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We drew out from every nation a witness﴾ [al-Qasas 75].

﴿And We drew out﴾: the naza' (drawing out) means extraction; drawing out a thing from a thing: removing it from it. ﴿And We drew out﴾ means (brought forth) ﴿from every nation﴾, and what is meant by "nation" (ummah) here is a group; but it is not merely any group. A group that was upon one method: this is called a nation (ummah); if a group is upon one method, it is called an ummah, and for this reason the letter "meem" indicating plurality and gathering came in it. So a state with many parties: is it a nation or not? In reality it is not a nation, because it is divided; but the nation is the group that gathered upon one method. For example, the nation of Islam is upon one religion; the nation of unbelief is upon one religion.

His saying: ﴿And We drew out from every nation a witness﴾: ﴿witness﴾ means a witnessing one, but it came in the form of intensive (mubalaghah) or in the form of the attributive adjective resembling the active participle.

And who is meant by the witness? The author says: (it is their prophet, who bears witness against them for what they said); this is what the author adopted.

And some scholars said: what is meant by the witness (shahid) is the ʿarīf (a leader, a chief appointed over a group), just as we say "ʿarīf"; that is, their leader and their chief, whom We extract from among them, and then We ask him this question, which is built on challenge: ﴿Bring your proof﴾ [al-Qasas 75]. This is also what our Shaykh ʿAbd al-Rahman (al-Saʿdi) went to in his tafsir: that what is meant by the witness here is the senior person of the community who is regarded as being in the position of an ʿarīf, because the senior person of the community is a representative of the community. Whatever the case, the closest view, and Allah knows best, is what our Shaykh held: that what is meant by the witness is one who is a witness among them and is regarded among them, so he is in the position of an ʿarīf.

(﴿So We will say﴾ to them, ﴿Bring your proof﴾.) Who is the speaker? Allah, glorified and exalted.

﴿Bring your proof﴾. Al-burhan (proof) means the evidence, i.e., bring the evidence (for what you claimed of association). Will they bring evidence or not?
* Student: They will not.
* Shaykh: Of course, they have no evidence.

His saying ﴿Bring﴾ is an imperative verb, and what is intended by it is challenge and also rebuke. Challenge, because it demands what is impossible; and rebuke, because there will befall them, before the people in that assembly, disgrace and shame that they cannot repel.

His saying ﴿So they will know that the truth belongs to Allah﴾ [al-Qasas 75]: when did they know that the truth belongs to Allah? When they did not bring evidence and proof for their association, they knew that they have no right in this association, and that the truth belongs to whom? ﴿The truth belongs to Allah﴾ alone, and that these idols have no right to worship, is that so?
* Student: Yes, indeed.
* Shaykh: These idols have no right to worship; ﴿that the truth﴾, meaning in worship, ﴿belongs to Allah﴾ alone.

Does this knowledge benefit them at that time or not? It does not benefit them, because on that day it is the day of recompense. It would have benefited them had they acted upon it in the world; had they known in the world that the truth belongs to Allah and then acted, that would have been beneficial to them. But after they have witnessed the punishment, their knowing that the truth belongs to Allah does not benefit them.

However, there is a great benefit in it. The great benefit in it is establishing the proof against them: ﴿Every time a group is thrown into it, its keepers ask them, "Did no warner come to you?" They say, "Yes indeed, a warner came to us, but we denied him and said, 'Allah has not sent down anything; you are only in great error.'" And they say, "Had we been listening or reasoning, we would not have been among the companions of the Blaze"﴾ [al-Mulk 8–10]. So the benefit of their being made to confess until it becomes clear to them that the truth belongs to Allah is that they know they were not wronged in anything.

﴿So they will know that the truth belongs to Allah, and that which they used to fabricate will vanish from them﴾ [al-Qasas 75]. Yes: (﴿the truth﴾ in divinity ﴿belongs to Allah﴾ alone, with no one sharing it with Him).

(﴿Vanished﴾: was absent ﴿from them, what they used to fabricate﴾ [al-Qasas 75] in the world, that they had a partner with them, exalted is Allah far above that.) (A partner) — what comes after it?
* Student: (Exalted is He above that).
* Shaykh: (Exalted is He above that)?

﴿And that which they used to fabricate vanished from them.﴾ ﴿Vanished﴾: the author says, "in the sense of 'was absent'," but ﴿ḍalla﴾ is more eloquent than "ghāba" (was absent), because ﴿ḍalla﴾ implies as if it is a sought-after matter that is pursued but they fail to attain it, like a lost thing (ḍāllah): if a person's camel or sheep goes astray, for example, he searches for it and does not find it, and that is harder on him in regret. Here, ﴿it vanished from them﴾ is as though it were a lost thing, precious to them, but they were unable to reach it.

His saying ﴿what they used to fabricate﴾ [al-Qasas 75]: ﴿mā﴾, what is its grammatical analysis (i'rab)?
* Student: A relative pronoun.
* Shaykh: A relative noun, the subject of (ḍalla), or not? The subject of (ḍalla)? Yes, the subject of (ḍalla). And where is the returning pronoun (ʿāʾid)?
* Student: Omitted.
* Shaykh: And the implied form?
* Student: They used to fabricate it.
* Shaykh: "What they used to fabricate it."

The author's saying "in the world": because ﴿kānū﴾ is a past-tense verb, so ﴿what they used to fabricate﴾, in the world, that there was with Allah a partner, this partner vanishes from them on the Day of Resurrection, and they cannot establish any proof for it.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 28, verse 73–75 (part 1 of 2):

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And out of His mercy He made for you the night and the day, that you may rest therein﴾ [al-Qasas 73].

"﴿And out of His mercy He made﴾": the prepositional phrase (al-jar wa'l-majrur) is connected to His saying ﴿He made﴾. That is, He made for you the night and the day so that you may rest therein, out of His mercy.

As for His saying ﴿out of His mercy﴾: the ﴿min﴾ (out of) here indicates causation (lil-sababiyyah), meaning: because of His mercy, or because of the mercy with which He, glorified and exalted is He, is described. Mercy is a real attribute established for Allah, glorified and exalted is He, and it is other than will (al-irada), other than the will to bestow favour, and other than bestowing favour. The People of the Sunnah and the Community (Ahl al-Sunnah wa'l-Jama'ah) say: mercy is a real attribute established for Allah, mighty and majestic is He, which is not like the mercy of the created beings. As for the Ash'ariyyah, they distort the meaning of mercy, reducing it to bestowing favour or the will to bestow favour, so they interpret it as the act, which is bestowing favour, or its willing; because they affirm the will, which is a attribute of meaning (sifah ma'nawiyyah) that they affirm. It has already passed us that they affirm from the attributes only seven attributes, among them the will. So they explain mercy as the will to bestow favour. Why? They say: because the will is indicated by both revelation (al-sam') and reason ('aql), and we do not affirm from Allah's attributes except what reason indicates. As for what reason does not indicate, it is obligatory for us to interpret it (ta'wil); and we say: we distort it (tahrif) according to their practice. They call it ta'wil, and we say it is tahrif. They say: what reason indicates of Allah's attributes we affirm, and what it does not indicate must be interpreted, and in the more correct sense, distorted.

What is the evidence of reason for the will? They say: reason indicates the will through specification (al-takhsis): the specification of created things. Every created thing has been specified with something. Is that not so? This one Allah willed to be hard, so he became hard; that one to be soft, so he became soft; this one to be tall, so he is tall; this one short, so he is short, and so on. This [indicates]—we say (...)—this indicates what? It indicates will; that is, the matter cannot be without will.

Why have you denied mercy? They say: because mercy is a softness that afflicts the heart, necessitating tenderness toward the created being or the one shown mercy. We say to them: this mercy you mention is only the mercy of created beings, whereas we affirm for Allah a mercy that is not like the mercy of created beings. Then we also take evidence for mercy from reason just as you took evidence for the will from reason. How many blessings does Allah, glorified and exalted is He, have upon us?

* Student: They cannot be counted.

* The Shaykh: They cannot be counted or enumerated. And how many relief from distresses does Allah, glorified and exalted is He, have? They cannot be counted or enumerated. What is the matter that necessitates these things, to bring blessings and repel calamities?

* Student: Mercy.

* The Shaykh: Mercy; because the hard one who does not show mercy (...) does not bring a blessing nor repel a calamity.

So then, inference from events in which blessings are brought and calamities repelled is clearer and more evident than inference from specification to the will; because the indication of specification to the will is understood only by individuals of people, but the indication of bringing benefits and repelling calamities to mercy is understood by all people, even the common man in his market: if he sees a man harsh toward his children, for example, he says: this one has no mercy in his heart; and if he sees that he constantly brings them good and repels evil from them, he says: this is a merciful person.

So the indication of reason for mercy is stronger than its indication for the will, and yet they affirm the will and do not affirm mercy.

They say: "﴿And out of His mercy﴾" — it is not possible to affirm for Allah an attribute that is mercy; rather we say: "﴿out of His mercy﴾" [al-Qasas 73] means out of His bestowing favour. "﴿He made for you the night...﴾" to the end [al-Qasas 73].

We say: "﴿out of His mercy﴾", the ﴿min﴾ is for causation. And ﴿His mercy﴾ is His attribute with which He is described eternally and everlastingly; for this reason He opened His Book with ﴿In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate﴾ [al-Fatihah 1], and joined His lordship with that: ﴿Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds (2), the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate﴾ [al-Fatihah 2, 3], as an indication that this lordship, all of it, is a lordship of mercy; it is not a lordship of vengeance and harshness, but a lordship of mercy. So how can we deny this great attribute of Allah's attributes and affirm what is less than it?

This indicates the contradiction of these negators (al-mu'attilah) among the Ash'ariyyah, the Mu'tazilah and others, and that they contradict themselves: they affirm for Allah from the attributes what reason indicates the affirmation of what is more worthy of it, and they deny from the attributes what reason indicates their affirmation.

"﴿out of His mercy He made for you﴾": ﴿made﴾ here means created (khalaqa), not "rendered" (sayyara); and for this reason it did not take two objects.

"﴿He made for you the night and the day﴾" [al-Qasas 73]: a night and a day alternating among you, over people.

("﴿that you may rest therein﴾" [al-Qasas 73], i.e., in the night; "﴿and that you may seek of His bounty﴾" in the day, for earning.)

His saying: ﴿that you may rest therein﴾: the lam is for causation (lil-ta'lil), meaning: for the sake of your resting therein. The existence of the effect does not necessarily entail the existence of the cause when the cause is not effective. For example: ﴿And I did not create the jinn and mankind except that they should worship Me﴾ [al-Dhariyat 56]. This is a final cause (illah gha'iyyah), and the existence of the effect does not necessarily entail the existence of the final cause; so the creation does not necessarily entail the existence of worship.

Likewise ﴿that you may rest therein﴾ is a final cause and not an effective cause, and the existence of the effect does not necessarily entail the existence of the final cause. For example, someone may say: we find some people who do not rest at night, is that correct or not? There are people who do not rest at night: one whose livelihood is at night, like guards, and one whose amusement is at night, like those idle people who sleep by day and stay up at night. We say: the existence of the effect, when the cause is final, does not necessarily entail the existence of the cause, just as if you said: I have brought you this camel so that you may ride it; perhaps you ride it, and perhaps you do not. I gave you the pen so that you may write with it; perhaps you write, and perhaps you do not.

His saying: ﴿that you may rest therein﴾: the author says: (you rest, you take comfort), since it is not from "sukna" (dwelling) but from "sukun" (rest).

Where is the nun in His saying ﴿li-taskunu﴾? The nun has been dropped.

* Student: (...).

* The Shaykh: The nun has been dropped, because the verb is in the subjunctive. Strangely, I have in my copy (litaskununahu) [you rest in it], in the explanation, and the commentator also explained it with his saying: (you take comfort in it). No, I seek Allah's forgiveness! That is the previous one.

("﴿that you may rest therein﴾", i.e., in the night) meaning you take comfort.

"﴿and that you may seek of His bounty﴾" [al-Qasas 73]: (seek) means (seek out).

His saying: "﴿of His bounty﴾" means: of His giving and provision (in the day, for earning).

In the verse here, is there a laff wa-nashr (a complex, interleaved figure) that is arranged or not arranged?

* Student: Not arranged.

* The Shaykh: ﴿He made for you the night and the day, that you may rest therein and that you may seek of His bounty﴾ [al-Qasas 73]?

* Student: Not arranged.

* The Shaykh: It is arranged.

* Student: How?

* The Shaykh: Yes, it began with the night and mentioned its benefit first: rest, and this is at night; so there is an arranged laff wa-nashr: ﴿the night and the day, that you may rest therein and that you may seek of His bounty﴾.

﴿that you may rest therein and that you may seek of His bounty and that perhaps you may be thankful﴾.

(Perhaps) here is for causation, i.e., for the sake of your thanking Allah, glorified and exalted is He, for His blessing. Thus Allah, glorified and exalted is He, mentioned the two causes: the legal (shar'iyyah) and the divine-decreed (qadariyyah). As for the decreed cause, what is it? The decreed cause in the creation of night and day: ﴿that you may rest therein﴾.

* Student: ﴿and that you may seek of His bounty﴾.

* The Shaykh: ﴿and that you may seek of His bounty﴾. And the legal cause?

* Student: ﴿and that perhaps you may be thankful﴾.

* The Shaykh: ﴿and that perhaps you may be thankful﴾. That you thank Allah, glorified and exalted is He, for what He has bestowed upon you of the alternation of night and day; because things are made clear by their opposites. If the night were perpetual and the day perpetual, no one would rest by night, nor seek bounty by day. But Allah, glorified and exalted is He, made that for the sake of rest, although there are other benefits besides the matter of ﴿that you may rest therein and that you may seek of His bounty﴾ [al-Qasas 73], which Allah mentioned in Surah al-Furqan: ﴿And He it is who made the night and the day to succeed one another, for whoever wishes to remember or wishes to be thankful﴾ [al-Furqan 62]. And in the authentic hadith: "Indeed Allah, the Exalted, extends His hand by night so that the one who sinned by day may repent, and He extends His hand by day so that the one who sinned by night may repent."[[Recorded by Muslim (2759/31) from the hadith of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, may Allah be pleased with him.]]

So the sum is that in the alternation of night and day there are great benefits that necessitate that we thank Allah, glorified and exalted is He, for them.

Know that thanks is by the heart, the tongue and the limbs:

As for thanks by the heart: it is that a person acknowledges in his heart that these blessings are from Allah alone, acknowledging completely, so that even if these blessings came through a cause, let him believe that the cause is from whom? From Allah; it is He who brought it into being, and so this blessing was obtained through it.

As for thanks by the tongue: it is praising Allah, the Exalted, as He deserves, whether for this blessing or for other than it. So praising Allah as He deserves for this blessing or for other blessings, all of that is included in thanks. On this basis, a person's saying: "Glory be to Allah, and praise be to Allah, and Allah is greatest" is considered thanks; and his saying when he eats food or drinks a drink: "Praise be to Allah" (meaning for this food or drink) is also considered thanks.

As for the third, which is the limbs: it is that a person performs obedience to Allah, whether related to this blessing or not; he uses this blessing to help him in obedience, or performs an act of obedience that is not related to this blessing.

"Blessings from me have benefited you in three ways: my hand, my tongue, and the hidden heart."

("My hand"): this is the limb. ("My tongue"): this is the speech of the tongue. ("And the hidden heart"): this is the acknowledgment of the heart.

If someone says: you mentioned that thanks by the tongue is praising Allah, the Exalted, whether it relates to this blessing or to other than it; does His saying, "But as for the blessing of your Lord, proclaim it" [al-Duha 11], fall under this?

* Student: Yes, it falls under it.

* The Shaykh: Yes, this falls under it: ﴿But as for the blessing of your Lord, proclaim it﴾, so it is included in these noble verses.

If someone says: does this necessitate boasting? We say: no, this is not by way of boasting, but by way of humility before Allah, and that these blessings are from Allah, as the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "I am the master of the children of Adam on the Day of Resurrection, and I say it without boasting."[[Recorded by al-Tirmidhi (3148) from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him.]]

Then Allah the Exalted said: (﴿And﴾ mention ﴿the day He calls them, and says﴾ [al-Qasas 74]). The author, by his estimate of (mention), informed us that the adverbial phrase ﴿and the day He calls them﴾ is connected to an implied verb whose estimate is (mention).

His saying: ﴿and the day He calls them﴾, i.e., Allah, and that is the Day of Resurrection, ﴿and says: "Where are My partners whom you used to claim?"﴾ [al-Qasas 62]. Do I think this has passed us? Yes, it passed us recently, and this is a repetition of the warning against shirk; meaning: remember also the calling a second time: ﴿and the day He calls them and says: "Where are My partners whom you used to claim?"﴾ [al-Qasas 62].

The meaning of ﴿My partners﴾: those whom you made partners to Me in creation, provision and management, or in worship?

* Student: In worship.

* The Shaykh: Yes, those who associated others with Allah when the Messenger was sent, in worship; and they acknowledged that Allah alone is the Creator and Provider. But among people there are those who also deny that and say: there is no lord, or say: these things were brought into being by pure nature. This too is a kind of shirk; the first is pure suspension (ta'til mahd): whoever denies a god altogether is purely a negator (mu'attil), and the second is a polytheist.

His saying: ﴿whom you used to claim﴾: the author said: (It was mentioned a second time so that there could be built upon it: ﴿And We drew out from every nation a witness﴾ [al-Qasas 75], i.e., brought forth, ﴿and their prophet is a witness against them for what they said. ﴿And We said: Bring your proof﴾ for what you claimed of association; ﴿then they will know that the truth belongs to Allah﴾ [al-Qasas 75], i.e., lordship belongs to Allah) to the end.

We stop here (...).

* Student: (...)?

* The Shaykh: No; because it is a statement. It is one of the limbs without doubt, but it is a statement, and therefore (...).

[Real and established for Allah in a perfect manner, and not like the mercy of created beings.]

(...)

For example, if it is said: mercy implies weakness and softness and the like, we say: that is with respect to the created being; it is a real mercy that is not like the mercy of created beings.

* Among its benefits: showing Allah's blessing in the alternation of night and day: ﴿out of His mercy He made for you the night and the day﴾ [al-Qasas 73].

* Among them: that the night is for rest and the day is for seeking livelihood; by His saying: ﴿that you may rest therein﴾ at night, ﴿and that you may seek of His bounty﴾ [al-Qasas 73] in the day.

* There branches from this matter a benefit, which is what the scholars (al-Ashab), may Allah have mercy on them, mentioned concerning the division between two wives: if a man has two wives and wishes to divide between them, is the basis of division the night or the day? The basis is the night for one whose livelihood is by day, and the day for one whose livelihood is by night; if the matter is unclear to us, the basis is the night, since it is the place of rest.

* Also among the benefits of the verse: that the night is the place of rest, and rest in it is in sleep; rest is more beneficial to the body than that by day.

* Also: affirmation of causes, in His saying: ﴿and that you may seek of His bounty﴾, i.e., that you may seek. Provision does not come down from heaven merely; rather there must be seeking. If you do not take this cause by which provision is obtained, provision will not come; because Allah, the Exalted, is Wise, and has linked causes to their effects. So in the verse ﴿and that you may seek of His bounty﴾ is the affirmation of causes, and that matters come by their causes.

* Among them: that provision is a favour from Allah, mighty and majestic is He, and bounty and gift: ﴿and that you may seek of His bounty﴾ [al-Qasas 73]. It is not obtained merely by a person's exertion and striving; how many a person strives and toils and yet his provision is narrow, and how many a person does fewer means than the first and then is granted abundance in provision.

* Among the benefits of the verse: the importance of thanks, by His saying: ﴿and that perhaps you may be thankful﴾ [al-Qasas 73].

* Among them: that it is fitting for a person to have insight into what Allah has subjected to him, so that he may thank Allah for it. Allah has subjected to us the night and the day, the sun and the moon; so let us take a lesson from this by which we arrive at thanking Allah, glorified and exalted is He, for that.

* * *

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And the day He calls them and says: "Where are My partners whom you used to claim?"﴾ [al-Qasas 74].

Is it taken from its benefits what preceded in the first verse, or not?

* Student: Yes.

* The Shaykh: Has this verse not passed us in its wording? Yes, it passed us in its wording, so its benefits are referred to what preceded.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We drew out from every nation a witness﴾ [al-Qasas 75].

﴿And We drew out﴾: the naza' (drawing out) means extraction; drawing out a thing from a thing: removing it from it. ﴿And We drew out﴾ means (brought forth) ﴿from every nation﴾, and what is meant by "nation" (ummah) here is a group; but it is not merely any group. A group that was upon one method: this is called a nation (ummah); if a group is upon one method, it is called an ummah, and for this reason the letter "meem" indicating plurality and gathering came in it. So a state with many parties: is it a nation or not? In reality it is not a nation, because it is divided; but the nation is the group that gathered upon one method. For example, the nation of Islam is upon one religion; the nation of unbelief is upon one religion.

His saying: ﴿And We drew out from every nation a witness﴾: ﴿witness﴾ means a witnessing one, but it came in the form of intensive (mubalaghah) or in the form of the attributive adjective resembling the active participle.

And who is meant by the witness? The author says: (it is their prophet, who bears witness against them for what they said); this is what the author adopted.

And some scholars said: what is meant by the witness (shahid) is the ʿarīf (a leader, a chief appointed over a group), just as we say "ʿarīf"; that is, their leader and their chief, whom We extract from among them, and then We ask him this question, which is built on challenge: ﴿Bring your proof﴾ [al-Qasas 75]. This is also what our Shaykh ʿAbd al-Rahman (al-Saʿdi) went to in his tafsir: that what is meant by the witness here is the senior person of the community who is regarded as being in the position of an ʿarīf, because the senior person of the community is a representative of the community. Whatever the case, the closest view, and Allah knows best, is what our Shaykh held: that what is meant by the witness is one who is a witness among them and is regarded among them, so he is in the position of an ʿarīf.

(﴿So We will say﴾ to them, ﴿Bring your proof﴾.) Who is the speaker? Allah, glorified and exalted.

﴿Bring your proof﴾. Al-burhan (proof) means the evidence, i.e., bring the evidence (for what you claimed of association). Will they bring evidence or not?
* Student: They will not.
* Shaykh: Of course, they have no evidence.

His saying ﴿Bring﴾ is an imperative verb, and what is intended by it is challenge and also rebuke. Challenge, because it demands what is impossible; and rebuke, because there will befall them, before the people in that assembly, disgrace and shame that they cannot repel.

His saying ﴿So they will know that the truth belongs to Allah﴾ [al-Qasas 75]: when did they know that the truth belongs to Allah? When they did not bring evidence and proof for their association, they knew that they have no right in this association, and that the truth belongs to whom? ﴿The truth belongs to Allah﴾ alone, and that these idols have no right to worship, is that so?
* Student: Yes, indeed.
* Shaykh: These idols have no right to worship; ﴿that the truth﴾, meaning in worship, ﴿belongs to Allah﴾ alone.

Does this knowledge benefit them at that time or not? It does not benefit them, because on that day it is the day of recompense. It would have benefited them had they acted upon it in the world; had they known in the world that the truth belongs to Allah and then acted, that would have been beneficial to them. But after they have witnessed the punishment, their knowing that the truth belongs to Allah does not benefit them.

However, there is a great benefit in it. The great benefit in it is establishing the proof against them: ﴿Every time a group is thrown into it, its keepers ask them, "Did no warner come to you?" They say, "Yes indeed, a warner came to us, but we denied him and said, 'Allah has not sent down anything; you are only in great error.'" And they say, "Had we been listening or reasoning, we would not have been among the companions of the Blaze"﴾ [al-Mulk 8–10]. So the benefit of their being made to confess until it becomes clear to them that the truth belongs to Allah is that they know they were not wronged in anything.

﴿So they will know that the truth belongs to Allah, and that which they used to fabricate will vanish from them﴾ [al-Qasas 75]. Yes: (﴿the truth﴾ in divinity ﴿belongs to Allah﴾ alone, with no one sharing it with Him).

(﴿Vanished﴾: was absent ﴿from them, what they used to fabricate﴾ [al-Qasas 75] in the world, that they had a partner with them, exalted is Allah far above that.) (A partner) — what comes after it?
* Student: (Exalted is He above that).
* Shaykh: (Exalted is He above that)?

﴿And that which they used to fabricate vanished from them.﴾ ﴿Vanished﴾: the author says, "in the sense of 'was absent'," but ﴿ḍalla﴾ is more eloquent than "ghāba" (was absent), because ﴿ḍalla﴾ implies as if it is a sought-after matter that is pursued but they fail to attain it, like a lost thing (ḍāllah): if a person's camel or sheep goes astray, for example, he searches for it and does not find it, and that is harder on him in regret. Here, ﴿it vanished from them﴾ is as though it were a lost thing, precious to them, but they were unable to reach it.

His saying ﴿what they used to fabricate﴾ [al-Qasas 75]: ﴿mā﴾, what is its grammatical analysis (i'rab)?
* Student: A relative pronoun.
* Shaykh: A relative noun, the subject of (ḍalla), or not? The subject of (ḍalla)? Yes, the subject of (ḍalla). And where is the returning pronoun (ʿāʾid)?
* Student: Omitted.
* Shaykh: And the implied form?
* Student: They used to fabricate it.
* Shaykh: "What they used to fabricate it."

The author's saying "in the world": because ﴿kānū﴾ is a past-tense verb, so ﴿what they used to fabricate﴾, in the world, that there was with Allah a partner, this partner vanishes from them on the Day of Resurrection, and they cannot establish any proof for it.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 28, verse 73–75 (part 1 of 2):

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And out of His mercy He made for you the night and the day, that you may rest therein﴾ [al-Qasas 73].

"﴿And out of His mercy He made﴾": the prepositional phrase (al-jar wa'l-majrur) is connected to His saying ﴿He made﴾. That is, He made for you the night and the day so that you may rest therein, out of His mercy.

As for His saying ﴿out of His mercy﴾: the ﴿min﴾ (out of) here indicates causation (lil-sababiyyah), meaning: because of His mercy, or because of the mercy with which He, glorified and exalted is He, is described. Mercy is a real attribute established for Allah, glorified and exalted is He, and it is other than will (al-irada), other than the will to bestow favour, and other than bestowing favour. The People of the Sunnah and the Community (Ahl al-Sunnah wa'l-Jama'ah) say: mercy is a real attribute established for Allah, mighty and majestic is He, which is not like the mercy of the created beings. As for the Ash'ariyyah, they distort the meaning of mercy, reducing it to bestowing favour or the will to bestow favour, so they interpret it as the act, which is bestowing favour, or its willing; because they affirm the will, which is a attribute of meaning (sifah ma'nawiyyah) that they affirm. It has already passed us that they affirm from the attributes only seven attributes, among them the will. So they explain mercy as the will to bestow favour. Why? They say: because the will is indicated by both revelation (al-sam') and reason ('aql), and we do not affirm from Allah's attributes except what reason indicates. As for what reason does not indicate, it is obligatory for us to interpret it (ta'wil); and we say: we distort it (tahrif) according to their practice. They call it ta'wil, and we say it is tahrif. They say: what reason indicates of Allah's attributes we affirm, and what it does not indicate must be interpreted, and in the more correct sense, distorted.

What is the evidence of reason for the will? They say: reason indicates the will through specification (al-takhsis): the specification of created things. Every created thing has been specified with something. Is that not so? This one Allah willed to be hard, so he became hard; that one to be soft, so he became soft; this one to be tall, so he is tall; this one short, so he is short, and so on. This [indicates]—we say (...)—this indicates what? It indicates will; that is, the matter cannot be without will.

Why have you denied mercy? They say: because mercy is a softness that afflicts the heart, necessitating tenderness toward the created being or the one shown mercy. We say to them: this mercy you mention is only the mercy of created beings, whereas we affirm for Allah a mercy that is not like the mercy of created beings. Then we also take evidence for mercy from reason just as you took evidence for the will from reason. How many blessings does Allah, glorified and exalted is He, have upon us?

* Student: They cannot be counted.

* The Shaykh: They cannot be counted or enumerated. And how many relief from distresses does Allah, glorified and exalted is He, have? They cannot be counted or enumerated. What is the matter that necessitates these things, to bring blessings and repel calamities?

* Student: Mercy.

* The Shaykh: Mercy; because the hard one who does not show mercy (...) does not bring a blessing nor repel a calamity.

So then, inference from events in which blessings are brought and calamities repelled is clearer and more evident than inference from specification to the will; because the indication of specification to the will is understood only by individuals of people, but the indication of bringing benefits and repelling calamities to mercy is understood by all people, even the common man in his market: if he sees a man harsh toward his children, for example, he says: this one has no mercy in his heart; and if he sees that he constantly brings them good and repels evil from them, he says: this is a merciful person.

So the indication of reason for mercy is stronger than its indication for the will, and yet they affirm the will and do not affirm mercy.

They say: "﴿And out of His mercy﴾" — it is not possible to affirm for Allah an attribute that is mercy; rather we say: "﴿out of His mercy﴾" [al-Qasas 73] means out of His bestowing favour. "﴿He made for you the night...﴾" to the end [al-Qasas 73].

We say: "﴿out of His mercy﴾", the ﴿min﴾ is for causation. And ﴿His mercy﴾ is His attribute with which He is described eternally and everlastingly; for this reason He opened His Book with ﴿In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate﴾ [al-Fatihah 1], and joined His lordship with that: ﴿Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds (2), the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate﴾ [al-Fatihah 2, 3], as an indication that this lordship, all of it, is a lordship of mercy; it is not a lordship of vengeance and harshness, but a lordship of mercy. So how can we deny this great attribute of Allah's attributes and affirm what is less than it?

This indicates the contradiction of these negators (al-mu'attilah) among the Ash'ariyyah, the Mu'tazilah and others, and that they contradict themselves: they affirm for Allah from the attributes what reason indicates the affirmation of what is more worthy of it, and they deny from the attributes what reason indicates their affirmation.

"﴿out of His mercy He made for you﴾": ﴿made﴾ here means created (khalaqa), not "rendered" (sayyara); and for this reason it did not take two objects.

"﴿He made for you the night and the day﴾" [al-Qasas 73]: a night and a day alternating among you, over people.

("﴿that you may rest therein﴾" [al-Qasas 73], i.e., in the night; "﴿and that you may seek of His bounty﴾" in the day, for earning.)

His saying: ﴿that you may rest therein﴾: the lam is for causation (lil-ta'lil), meaning: for the sake of your resting therein. The existence of the effect does not necessarily entail the existence of the cause when the cause is not effective. For example: ﴿And I did not create the jinn and mankind except that they should worship Me﴾ [al-Dhariyat 56]. This is a final cause (illah gha'iyyah), and the existence of the effect does not necessarily entail the existence of the final cause; so the creation does not necessarily entail the existence of worship.

Likewise ﴿that you may rest therein﴾ is a final cause and not an effective cause, and the existence of the effect does not necessarily entail the existence of the final cause. For example, someone may say: we find some people who do not rest at night, is that correct or not? There are people who do not rest at night: one whose livelihood is at night, like guards, and one whose amusement is at night, like those idle people who sleep by day and stay up at night. We say: the existence of the effect, when the cause is final, does not necessarily entail the existence of the cause, just as if you said: I have brought you this camel so that you may ride it; perhaps you ride it, and perhaps you do not. I gave you the pen so that you may write with it; perhaps you write, and perhaps you do not.

His saying: ﴿that you may rest therein﴾: the author says: (you rest, you take comfort), since it is not from "sukna" (dwelling) but from "sukun" (rest).

Where is the nun in His saying ﴿li-taskunu﴾? The nun has been dropped.

* Student: (...).

* The Shaykh: The nun has been dropped, because the verb is in the subjunctive. Strangely, I have in my copy (litaskununahu) [you rest in it], in the explanation, and the commentator also explained it with his saying: (you take comfort in it). No, I seek Allah's forgiveness! That is the previous one.

("﴿that you may rest therein﴾", i.e., in the night) meaning you take comfort.

"﴿and that you may seek of His bounty﴾" [al-Qasas 73]: (seek) means (seek out).

His saying: "﴿of His bounty﴾" means: of His giving and provision (in the day, for earning).

In the verse here, is there a laff wa-nashr (a complex, interleaved figure) that is arranged or not arranged?

* Student: Not arranged.

* The Shaykh: ﴿He made for you the night and the day, that you may rest therein and that you may seek of His bounty﴾ [al-Qasas 73]?

* Student: Not arranged.

* The Shaykh: It is arranged.

* Student: How?

* The Shaykh: Yes, it began with the night and mentioned its benefit first: rest, and this is at night; so there is an arranged laff wa-nashr: ﴿the night and the day, that you may rest therein and that you may seek of His bounty﴾.

﴿that you may rest therein and that you may seek of His bounty and that perhaps you may be thankful﴾.

(Perhaps) here is for causation, i.e., for the sake of your thanking Allah, glorified and exalted is He, for His blessing. Thus Allah, glorified and exalted is He, mentioned the two causes: the legal (shar'iyyah) and the divine-decreed (qadariyyah). As for the decreed cause, what is it? The decreed cause in the creation of night and day: ﴿that you may rest therein﴾.

* Student: ﴿and that you may seek of His bounty﴾.

* The Shaykh: ﴿and that you may seek of His bounty﴾. And the legal cause?

* Student: ﴿and that perhaps you may be thankful﴾.

* The Shaykh: ﴿and that perhaps you may be thankful﴾. That you thank Allah, glorified and exalted is He, for what He has bestowed upon you of the alternation of night and day; because things are made clear by their opposites. If the night were perpetual and the day perpetual, no one would rest by night, nor seek bounty by day. But Allah, glorified and exalted is He, made that for the sake of rest, although there are other benefits besides the matter of ﴿that you may rest therein and that you may seek of His bounty﴾ [al-Qasas 73], which Allah mentioned in Surah al-Furqan: ﴿And He it is who made the night and the day to succeed one another, for whoever wishes to remember or wishes to be thankful﴾ [al-Furqan 62]. And in the authentic hadith: "Indeed Allah, the Exalted, extends His hand by night so that the one who sinned by day may repent, and He extends His hand by day so that the one who sinned by night may repent."[[Recorded by Muslim (2759/31) from the hadith of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, may Allah be pleased with him.]]

So the sum is that in the alternation of night and day there are great benefits that necessitate that we thank Allah, glorified and exalted is He, for them.

Know that thanks is by the heart, the tongue and the limbs:

As for thanks by the heart: it is that a person acknowledges in his heart that these blessings are from Allah alone, acknowledging completely, so that even if these blessings came through a cause, let him believe that the cause is from whom? From Allah; it is He who brought it into being, and so this blessing was obtained through it.

As for thanks by the tongue: it is praising Allah, the Exalted, as He deserves, whether for this blessing or for other than it. So praising Allah as He deserves for this blessing or for other blessings, all of that is included in thanks. On this basis, a person's saying: "Glory be to Allah, and praise be to Allah, and Allah is greatest" is considered thanks; and his saying when he eats food or drinks a drink: "Praise be to Allah" (meaning for this food or drink) is also considered thanks.

As for the third, which is the limbs: it is that a person performs obedience to Allah, whether related to this blessing or not; he uses this blessing to help him in obedience, or performs an act of obedience that is not related to this blessing.

"Blessings from me have benefited you in three ways: my hand, my tongue, and the hidden heart."

("My hand"): this is the limb. ("My tongue"): this is the speech of the tongue. ("And the hidden heart"): this is the acknowledgment of the heart.

If someone says: you mentioned that thanks by the tongue is praising Allah, the Exalted, whether it relates to this blessing or to other than it; does His saying, "But as for the blessing of your Lord, proclaim it" [al-Duha 11], fall under this?

* Student: Yes, it falls under it.

* The Shaykh: Yes, this falls under it: ﴿But as for the blessing of your Lord, proclaim it﴾, so it is included in these noble verses.

If someone says: does this necessitate boasting? We say: no, this is not by way of boasting, but by way of humility before Allah, and that these blessings are from Allah, as the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "I am the master of the children of Adam on the Day of Resurrection, and I say it without boasting."[[Recorded by al-Tirmidhi (3148) from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him.]]

Then Allah the Exalted said: (﴿And﴾ mention ﴿the day He calls them, and says﴾ [al-Qasas 74]). The author, by his estimate of (mention), informed us that the adverbial phrase ﴿and the day He calls them﴾ is connected to an implied verb whose estimate is (mention).

His saying: ﴿and the day He calls them﴾, i.e., Allah, and that is the Day of Resurrection, ﴿and says: "Where are My partners whom you used to claim?"﴾ [al-Qasas 62]. Do I think this has passed us? Yes, it passed us recently, and this is a repetition of the warning against shirk; meaning: remember also the calling a second time: ﴿and the day He calls them and says: "Where are My partners whom you used to claim?"﴾ [al-Qasas 62].

The meaning of ﴿My partners﴾: those whom you made partners to Me in creation, provision and management, or in worship?

* Student: In worship.

* The Shaykh: Yes, those who associated others with Allah when the Messenger was sent, in worship; and they acknowledged that Allah alone is the Creator and Provider. But among people there are those who also deny that and say: there is no lord, or say: these things were brought into being by pure nature. This too is a kind of shirk; the first is pure suspension (ta'til mahd): whoever denies a god altogether is purely a negator (mu'attil), and the second is a polytheist.

His saying: ﴿whom you used to claim﴾: the author said: (It was mentioned a second time so that there could be built upon it: ﴿And We drew out from every nation a witness﴾ [al-Qasas 75], i.e., brought forth, ﴿and their prophet is a witness against them for what they said. ﴿And We said: Bring your proof﴾ for what you claimed of association; ﴿then they will know that the truth belongs to Allah﴾ [al-Qasas 75], i.e., lordship belongs to Allah) to the end.

We stop here (...).

* Student: (...)?

* The Shaykh: No; because it is a statement. It is one of the limbs without doubt, but it is a statement, and therefore (...).

[Real and established for Allah in a perfect manner, and not like the mercy of created beings.]

(...)

For example, if it is said: mercy implies weakness and softness and the like, we say: that is with respect to the created being; it is a real mercy that is not like the mercy of created beings.

* Among its benefits: showing Allah's blessing in the alternation of night and day: ﴿out of His mercy He made for you the night and the day﴾ [al-Qasas 73].

* Among them: that the night is for rest and the day is for seeking livelihood; by His saying: ﴿that you may rest therein﴾ at night, ﴿and that you may seek of His bounty﴾ [al-Qasas 73] in the day.

* There branches from this matter a benefit, which is what the scholars (al-Ashab), may Allah have mercy on them, mentioned concerning the division between two wives: if a man has two wives and wishes to divide between them, is the basis of division the night or the day? The basis is the night for one whose livelihood is by day, and the day for one whose livelihood is by night; if the matter is unclear to us, the basis is the night, since it is the place of rest.

* Also among the benefits of the verse: that the night is the place of rest, and rest in it is in sleep; rest is more beneficial to the body than that by day.

* Also: affirmation of causes, in His saying: ﴿and that you may seek of His bounty﴾, i.e., that you may seek. Provision does not come down from heaven merely; rather there must be seeking. If you do not take this cause by which provision is obtained, provision will not come; because Allah, the Exalted, is Wise, and has linked causes to their effects. So in the verse ﴿and that you may seek of His bounty﴾ is the affirmation of causes, and that matters come by their causes.

* Among them: that provision is a favour from Allah, mighty and majestic is He, and bounty and gift: ﴿and that you may seek of His bounty﴾ [al-Qasas 73]. It is not obtained merely by a person's exertion and striving; how many a person strives and toils and yet his provision is narrow, and how many a person does fewer means than the first and then is granted abundance in provision.

* Among the benefits of the verse: the importance of thanks, by His saying: ﴿and that perhaps you may be thankful﴾ [al-Qasas 73].

* Among them: that it is fitting for a person to have insight into what Allah has subjected to him, so that he may thank Allah for it. Allah has subjected to us the night and the day, the sun and the moon; so let us take a lesson from this by which we arrive at thanking Allah, glorified and exalted is He, for that.

* * *

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And the day He calls them and says: "Where are My partners whom you used to claim?"﴾ [al-Qasas 74].

Is it taken from its benefits what preceded in the first verse, or not?

* Student: Yes.

* The Shaykh: Has this verse not passed us in its wording? Yes, it passed us in its wording, so its benefits are referred to what preceded.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We drew out from every nation a witness﴾ [al-Qasas 75].

﴿And We drew out﴾: the naza' (drawing out) means extraction; drawing out a thing from a thing: removing it from it. ﴿And We drew out﴾ means (brought forth) ﴿from every nation﴾, and what is meant by "nation" (ummah) here is a group; but it is not merely any group. A group that was upon one method: this is called a nation (ummah); if a group is upon one method, it is called an ummah, and for this reason the letter "meem" indicating plurality and gathering came in it. So a state with many parties: is it a nation or not? In reality it is not a nation, because it is divided; but the nation is the group that gathered upon one method. For example, the nation of Islam is upon one religion; the nation of unbelief is upon one religion.

His saying: ﴿And We drew out from every nation a witness﴾: ﴿witness﴾ means a witnessing one, but it came in the form of intensive (mubalaghah) or in the form of the attributive adjective resembling the active participle.

And who is meant by the witness? The author says: (it is their prophet, who bears witness against them for what they said); this is what the author adopted.

And some scholars said: what is meant by the witness (shahid) is the ʿarīf (a leader, a chief appointed over a group), just as we say "ʿarīf"; that is, their leader and their chief, whom We extract from among them, and then We ask him this question, which is built on challenge: ﴿Bring your proof﴾ [al-Qasas 75]. This is also what our Shaykh ʿAbd al-Rahman (al-Saʿdi) went to in his tafsir: that what is meant by the witness here is the senior person of the community who is regarded as being in the position of an ʿarīf, because the senior person of the community is a representative of the community. Whatever the case, the closest view, and Allah knows best, is what our Shaykh held: that what is meant by the witness is one who is a witness among them and is regarded among them, so he is in the position of an ʿarīf.

(﴿So We will say﴾ to them, ﴿Bring your proof﴾.) Who is the speaker? Allah, glorified and exalted.

﴿Bring your proof﴾. Al-burhan (proof) means the evidence, i.e., bring the evidence (for what you claimed of association). Will they bring evidence or not?
* Student: They will not.
* Shaykh: Of course, they have no evidence.

His saying ﴿Bring﴾ is an imperative verb, and what is intended by it is challenge and also rebuke. Challenge, because it demands what is impossible; and rebuke, because there will befall them, before the people in that assembly, disgrace and shame that they cannot repel.

His saying ﴿So they will know that the truth belongs to Allah﴾ [al-Qasas 75]: when did they know that the truth belongs to Allah? When they did not bring evidence and proof for their association, they knew that they have no right in this association, and that the truth belongs to whom? ﴿The truth belongs to Allah﴾ alone, and that these idols have no right to worship, is that so?
* Student: Yes, indeed.
* Shaykh: These idols have no right to worship; ﴿that the truth﴾, meaning in worship, ﴿belongs to Allah﴾ alone.

Does this knowledge benefit them at that time or not? It does not benefit them, because on that day it is the day of recompense. It would have benefited them had they acted upon it in the world; had they known in the world that the truth belongs to Allah and then acted, that would have been beneficial to them. But after they have witnessed the punishment, their knowing that the truth belongs to Allah does not benefit them.

However, there is a great benefit in it. The great benefit in it is establishing the proof against them: ﴿Every time a group is thrown into it, its keepers ask them, "Did no warner come to you?" They say, "Yes indeed, a warner came to us, but we denied him and said, 'Allah has not sent down anything; you are only in great error.'" And they say, "Had we been listening or reasoning, we would not have been among the companions of the Blaze"﴾ [al-Mulk 8–10]. So the benefit of their being made to confess until it becomes clear to them that the truth belongs to Allah is that they know they were not wronged in anything.

﴿So they will know that the truth belongs to Allah, and that which they used to fabricate will vanish from them﴾ [al-Qasas 75]. Yes: (﴿the truth﴾ in divinity ﴿belongs to Allah﴾ alone, with no one sharing it with Him).

(﴿Vanished﴾: was absent ﴿from them, what they used to fabricate﴾ [al-Qasas 75] in the world, that they had a partner with them, exalted is Allah far above that.) (A partner) — what comes after it?
* Student: (Exalted is He above that).
* Shaykh: (Exalted is He above that)?

﴿And that which they used to fabricate vanished from them.﴾ ﴿Vanished﴾: the author says, "in the sense of 'was absent'," but ﴿ḍalla﴾ is more eloquent than "ghāba" (was absent), because ﴿ḍalla﴾ implies as if it is a sought-after matter that is pursued but they fail to attain it, like a lost thing (ḍāllah): if a person's camel or sheep goes astray, for example, he searches for it and does not find it, and that is harder on him in regret. Here, ﴿it vanished from them﴾ is as though it were a lost thing, precious to them, but they were unable to reach it.

His saying ﴿what they used to fabricate﴾ [al-Qasas 75]: ﴿mā﴾, what is its grammatical analysis (i'rab)?
* Student: A relative pronoun.
* Shaykh: A relative noun, the subject of (ḍalla), or not? The subject of (ḍalla)? Yes, the subject of (ḍalla). And where is the returning pronoun (ʿāʾid)?
* Student: Omitted.
* Shaykh: And the implied form?
* Student: They used to fabricate it.
* Shaykh: "What they used to fabricate it."

The author's saying "in the world": because ﴿kānū﴾ is a past-tense verb, so ﴿what they used to fabricate﴾, in the world, that there was with Allah a partner, this partner vanishes from them on the Day of Resurrection, and they cannot establish any proof for it.

Almighty Allah says: ﴿Indeed, Qarun was among the people of Musa﴾ [al-Qasas 76].

﴿Qarun﴾ is the name of a wealthy man from the Children of Israel. The author said: "[He was] among his relatives" (من أقاربه). Here he interpreted "people" (القوم) as "relatives," and then said: "He was his paternal cousin and his maternal cousin" (إنه ابن عمه وابن خالته). How is that (ابن عمه وابن خالته)? What does it look like? Draw it for me.

* Student: Two brothers married two sisters.

* Shaykh: Two brothers married two sisters; each of them then fathered a child, and these two children would be paternal cousin and maternal cousin to each other. But this is a claim whose soundness we do not know. It was said that he was his paternal cousin, and it was said that he was "from his people," meaning from the Children of Israel, since the Children of Israel are the people of Musa. We are not concerned whether he was closely related to Musa or distantly related; what matters is his story that took place, and that this man was from the people of Musa.

(He believed in him, "so he oppressed them" (فَبَغَى عَلَيْهِمْ) through arrogance, haughtiness and abundance of wealth.) The "ba'" (الباء) here indicates cause. ﴿So he oppressed them﴾ means he transgressed and acted superciliously toward them. Toward whom? Toward the people of Musa. ﴿He was from the people of Musa, so he oppressed them﴾ [al-Qasas 76], that is, toward these people. Because of the wealth Allah had given him, he became a tyrant, and this is the nature of a human being as a human being. Allah says: ﴿Nay! Indeed, man does transgress (6), when he sees himself self-sufficient﴾ [al-Alaq 6-7]. So this person, when his wealth increases and he sees himself as independent of others, becomes tyrannical, we seek refuge in Allah.

﴿And We gave him﴾.

* Student: Where is (...)?

* Shaykh: The "ba'" in his saying "(with arrogance)."

He says: ﴿And We gave him of the treasures﴾ [al-Qasas 76]. ﴿And We gave him﴾ means We bestowed upon him ﴿of the treasures﴾, that is, of treasures of wealth. It is the plural of "kanz" (كنز), and a kanz is what is kept hidden and locked up. It includes all kinds of wealth: gold, silver, emeralds, jewels, cash and other things.

These treasures: ﴿مَا إِنَّ﴾, "مَا" is a relative pronoun, and it is the second object of (آتيناه). What is its first object?

* Student: (...).

* Shaykh: No, the pronoun: the "hā'" in ﴿وَآتَيْنَاهُ﴾.

And his saying "مَا" means "that which" ﴿Indeed, its keys would weigh down a band of men of great strength﴾ [al-Qasas 76].

﴿إِنَّ﴾ is a particle of emphasis that puts the subject in the accusative and the predicate in the nominative. "Mafatih" (مفاتح) is its noun, and the clause ﴿لَتَنُوءُ﴾ is its predicate. The clause consisting of ﴿إِنَّ﴾ with its noun and predicate is the relative clause of "مَا," meaning "that which": ﴿Indeed, its keys﴾. "Tanu'" means: the keys weigh heavily upon them. "Mafatih" is the plural of "mifatah," which is the name for a key.

The author said: (﴿لَتَنُوءُ﴾ weighs down, ﴿بِالْعُصْبَةِ﴾ the group, ﴿أُولِي﴾ people of ﴿الْقُوَّةِ﴾ strength, that is, weighs them down; the "ba'" is for transitivity.)

The "ba'" in his saying ﴿بِالْعُصْبَةِ﴾ is used to make the verb transitive to its object through a preposition. The author needed to mention this because (ناء، ينوء) can be transitive either directly or through a preposition, and here it is transitive through a preposition.

(That is, it weighs them down; the "ba'" is for transitivity. As for their number, it was said: seventy, it was said: forty, it was said: ten, and other things were said.) The number of the "'usbah." There is no doubt that the "'usbah" is the group whose members support one another. "Asb" in the language means binding, and from it they called relatives "'asabah," because they strengthen the arm of their relative.

So they are the group possessing strength. Some scholars say: from three to seven; some say up to ten; and some, as the author said, say seventy or forty. The matter is subject to disagreement, but what appears to us is that they are the group who bind one another together, and they must be numerous; there is no need to define their exact number.

Yet, together with being a united group, they were people of strength, so two things combined in their case: strength in quality and number in quantity. So they had both quantity and quality. If this group gathered only to carry the keys, just the keys, the keys would weigh them down. We might say, for example: "This cannot be lifted by ten," meaning its keys cannot be lifted by ten strong men. If that is so, what about the treasuries themselves? These are the keys of the treasuries, so what about what is in those treasuries? Meaning (...) a great deal, which Allah, glorified and exalted, had given him.

﴿When his people said to him﴾: (Remember ﴿when his people said to him﴾, the believers among the Children of Israel, ﴿Do not exult﴾ [al-Qasas 76] in the abundance of wealth, the exultation of insolence.)

﴿When his people said to him﴾, the sincere advisers to him, and they, as the author said, were "the believers," because only a believing man gives advice of this kind.

In the phrase ﴿when his people said to him﴾, the attribution (إضافة) shows that these people were very sincere in advising him, because whoever is of your own people is unlikely to deceive you, and must be a sincere adviser to you.

As for his saying ﴿لَا تَفْرَحْ﴾, is "لا" negating or prohibiting?

* Student: Prohibiting.

* Shaykh: What is the evidence?

* Student: The jussive.

* Shaykh: The verb is in the jussive, yes. ﴿Do not exult﴾. Exultation is of two kinds: joy that is gladness not carrying a person to pride and insolence, but rather leading a person to contentment with Allah's blessing and to fulfilling what Allah has made obligatory concerning it; and second, exultation of insolence, arrogance, transgression and oppression. This is the exultation from which these people forbade Qarun.

﴿Indeed, Allah does not love the exultant﴾. Here, is the meaning "He does not love" and "He does not dislike," or does negating love establish its opposite? Yes, it is by way of systematic examination and division: a person either exults, or does not exult, or dislikes; I mean: he loves, or does not love, or dislikes, or not?

* Student: Yes.

* Shaykh: A person either loves a thing, or dislikes a thing, or neither loves nor dislikes it. When Allah says: ﴿And Allah does not love every arrogant boaster﴾ [al-Hadid 23], ﴿Indeed, Allah does not love the exultant﴾ [al-Qasas 76], ﴿And Allah does not love corruption﴾ [al-Baqarah 205], is the meaning only the negation of love, such that what love is negated for is neither loved nor disliked by Allah, or is the intended meaning the affirmation of its opposite?

* Student: Affirmation of its opposite.

* Shaykh: Apparently, and Allah knows best, the intended meaning is affirming its opposite, although rational division does not require this, but the context requires it. Because everything that Allah says He does not love, we find it is among what Allah dislikes: ﴿And Allah does not love the corrupters﴾ [al-Ma'idah 64], ﴿does not love corruption﴾ [al-Baqarah 205], ﴿does not love every arrogant boaster﴾ [Luqman 18], ﴿does not love the wasteful﴾ [al-An'am 141], ﴿does not love the exultant﴾ [al-Qasas 76]. So the apparent meaning from the contexts is: what is intended? The affirmation of dislike. But He expressed it by negating love, because love is something beloved; so it is as if one who loves corruption, or loves exultation and the like, is met with the opposite of his aim.

As for his saying "(﴿الْفَرِحِينَ﴾ with that)": the referent is abundance of wealth, "with that" meaning with abundance of wealth. The exultation whose love Allah negated is the exultation of insolence and arrogance.

If someone asks: what is the reconciliation between His saying here ﴿Indeed, Allah does not love the exultant﴾ [al-Qasas 76], and His saying: ﴿Say: "By the grace of Allah and His mercy, let them rejoice; it is better than what they accumulate"﴾ [Yunus 58]?

We say: the meaning of His saying ﴿By the grace of Allah and His mercy, let them rejoice; it is better than what they accumulate﴾ is rejoicing in Allah's grace: the religion, knowledge and faith. For this reason He said ﴿it is better﴾ than what? ﴿than what they accumulate﴾ of the worldly life. This shows that the exultation He commanded is that a person rejoice in what Allah has bestowed upon him of knowledge and faith. It is established from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "Whoever is pleased by his good deed and saddened by his bad deed, that is the believer." As for the exultation whose possessor is not praised, it is rejoicing in the world in the manner of insolence and arrogance.

Rejoicing in the world in the sense that something pleasing has happened to a person, without insolence, is not objectionable. "'Amr ibn Salamah al-Jarmi said, when his people clothed him in a garment: 'I have not rejoiced in anything after Islam as I rejoiced in this garment'" (or he said: "in this garment"), is it not so?

* Student: Yes indeed.

* Shaykh: "'Aishah said: 'That I had asked the Prophet ﷺ permission as Sawdah asked him (meaning regarding departing from Muzdalifah) is more beloved to me than something I rejoice in.'"

So natural joy that does not lead to insolence, exultation and pride is something a person is not blamed for. Rather, when one rejoices in it, because it is a means to a legislated objective, one is praised for it and rewarded for it, such as rejoicing in wealth that has come to him because he loves to spend it in the way of Allah, in seeking knowledge, in building mosques, or in giving charity to the poor. This joy is praiseworthy.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 28, verse 77 (part 1 of 6):

(﴿And seek, through what Allah has given you, the Abode of the Hereafter﴾ [al-Qasas 77]: seek, through the wealth, by spending it in obedience to Allah).

﴿And seek﴾, i.e., seek. ﴿Through what﴾: through that which ﴿Allah has given you﴾, meaning, bestowed upon you. From where?

* Student: From wealth.

* The Shaykh: From wealth, from these great treasures whose keys would weigh down a band of strong men. Seek with them ﴿the Abode of the Hereafter﴾. The intended meaning of ﴿the Abode of the Hereafter﴾ here is Paradise, yes. ﴿That is the Abode of the Hereafter; We make it for those who do not desire haughtiness upon the earth or corruption, and the good outcome is for the righteous﴾ [al-Qasas 83]. And how is one to seek the Abode of the Hereafter through it?

The author, may Allah have mercy on him, said: (by spending it in obedience to Allah). Then that becomes what? A treasure for you with Allah in the Hereafter. And when a person trains himself to this and makes himself desire it, upon this matter, it becomes a disposition for him: he rejoices in it, is gladdened by it, and his soul takes delight in it. For this reason, the generous person's most beloved thing is giving. Ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah have mercy on him, mentioned in Zad al-Ma'ad that spending for Allah, the Most High, spending for Allah in Allah's cause, meaning within the limits of the Sharia, is among the greatest causes of the expansion of the chest. This is a known matter: you find that the most expansive of hearts are the generous, and that when a person gives a gift to someone he finds joy and expansion through it.

So if he applies this and seeks through it ﴿the Abode of the Hereafter﴾ [al-Qasas 77], then that will not be lost on him with Allah. Then, along with that, the advisers say to him: (﴿And do not forget﴾ [al-Qasas 77]: do not abandon). This is because forgetting is applied to two matters: one of them is heedlessness regarding a known thing which one had known and then became heedless of; and the second is abandonment. Here, ﴿and do not forget﴾ means: and do not abandon. From this also is His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿They forgot Allah, so He forgot them﴾ [al-Tawbah 67]. What is the meaning of "they forgot Allah"? They abandoned Him and did not fulfill His right. ﴿So He forgot them﴾: the Exalted abandoned them and did not reward them. And from it is His saying: ﴿And do not be like those who forgot Allah﴾, i.e., abandoned Him, ﴿so He caused them to forget themselves﴾ [al-Hashr 19], i.e., made them forget them, neglect them, and abandon them without attending to their rights.

As for His saying: ﴿Allah has enumerated it, but they forgot it﴾ [al-Mujadila 6], the intended meaning of forgetting here is heedlessness regarding a known thing: Allah has counted it, but they forgot it.

So from these two Qur'anic proofs it becomes clear to us that forgetting is applied to two meanings: one of them is abandonment, and the second is heedlessness regarding a known thing. Which of the two is more fitting to be attributed to Allah?

* Student: Abandonment.

* The Shaykh: Abandonment. As for heedlessness, Allah has negated it from Himself, saying: ﴿In a Book; my Lord neither errs nor forgets﴾ [Ta-Ha 52]. This is forgetting of what kind: heedlessness or abandonment?

* Student: Heedlessness.

* The Shaykh: Heedlessness, not abandonment, because Allah abandons whom He wills of His servants who deserve to be abandoned.

His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿And We had already taken a covenant from Adam before, but he forgot, and We found in him no determination﴾ [Ta-Ha 115]. Which of the two types?

* Student: Heedlessness.

* The Shaykh: Heedlessness, or abandonment?

* Student: No, abandonment, O Shaykh.

* The Shaykh: That is, when Adam, peace be upon him, ate from the tree, was he forgetful?

* Student: Had he been forgetful, he would not have been removed from it; Allah would not have held him accountable for it.

* The Shaykh: Yes, Allah did not hold him accountable for it. What do you say? This matter has two opinions among the scholars. Some of them said: His saying ﴿he forgot﴾ means he abandoned it deliberately, so he deserves punishment. According to this view there is no difficulty in the matter: that he is punished for a matter he abandoned without heedlessness, abandoned while knowing it. And he would be blameworthy, or not?

* Student: Yes.

* The Shaykh: He would be blameworthy, and for this reason He said: ﴿and We found in him no determination﴾ [Ta-Ha 115].

Others said: the intended meaning of forgetting is heedlessness. These intended by this to avoid describing Adam as deliberately committing disobedience, because if he abandoned it out of forgetting, that is heedlessness, is he blamed or not blamed?

* Student: Not blamed.

* The Shaykh: Not blamed. These need to answer the question of the lapse of sin through forgetting, and they say: this is among the special features of this community, the lapse of sin through forgetting, based on the saying of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him: "Indeed Allah has overlooked for my community error and forgetfulness" [narrated by Ibn Majah (2043) from Abu Dharr]. His saying "for my community" indicates that earlier nations were held accountable for it. And that earlier nations were also held accountable does not, in reality, favor either opinion. But what favors that it is forgetting of abandonment, not forgetting of heedlessness, is His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿And Adam disobeyed his Lord and went astray﴾ [Ta-Ha 121]. These two descriptions, disobedience and going astray, indicate that he did it deliberately. However, he was deceived by the deception of Iblis: ﴿So he brought them down by deception﴾ [al-A'raf 22], when he swore to them, ﴿Indeed, I am for you of the sincere advisers﴾ [al-A'raf 21], and said: ﴿Shall I direct you to the tree of eternity and a kingdom that does not decay?﴾ [Ta-Ha 120]. So Adam was deceived and did what he did.

The point is that forgetting here, His saying ﴿and do not forget﴾, is of which of the two types? It is abandonment.

﴿And do not forget your share of this world﴾ [al-Qasas 77]. He said ﴿and do not forget﴾ as if they are saying: make your absorption in what you seek in the Hereafter so complete that what you want for this world seems to vanish from you, but do not forget it.

As for his saying: (﴿your share of this world﴾, i.e., that you work in it for the Hereafter), the author indicates that the intended meaning of "your share of this world" refers back to His saying: ﴿And seek, through what Allah has given you, the Abode of the Hereafter﴾ [al-Qasas 77]. That is, ﴿and do not forget your share of this world﴾ [al-Qasas 77], by Our granting you a respite. So since you have been given a respite, do not forget this respite to spend wealth in obedience to Allah. The intended meaning of the share of this world here is then the living in this world; that is: do not forget to seize the opportunity in this world and spend. Thus the sentence here refers back to the first sentence in meaning; that is: seek the Abode of the Hereafter through what you spend, so that time is not lost to you and your share of this world is not lost.

For this reason he said: (﴿And do not forget your share of this world﴾, i.e., that you work in it for the Hereafter), as if he says: seize this period, which is your share of this world, and seize it for the Hereafter, so the second sentence refers back to the first.

And it is possible, and this is closer, that ﴿and do not forget your share of this world﴾ means that We do not command you to spend all your wealth on the Hereafter, but rather seek the Hereafter through it, and take your share of this world for yourself. We do not want you to strip yourself of your wealth, but We want you to seek through it ﴿the Abode of the Hereafter﴾. Nevertheless, take ﴿your share of this world﴾ of good food, cleanliness of home, clothing, wives, and the like. This meaning is closer and more correct, because on the meaning the author adopted the verse would contain some repetition.

Then, does this become a means of bringing him to accept the advice? Or do we say that if it is said to him, "seek the Hereafter and do not forget your portion of this world," this is closer to acceptance of the advice?

* Student: The latter.

* The Shaykh: The latter is closer, because if it were said: "This great wealth whose keys would weigh down a band of strong men, seek with all of it the Abode of the Hereafter," perhaps he would not accept. But if it is said: "Seek with it the Hereafter and enjoy a portion of this world," this is more likely to be accepted. It is also among the good methods of calling to Allah, the Most High. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said to Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As: "Indeed your Lord has a right over you, and your self has a right over you" [al-Bukhari (6134) from Abdullah ibn Amr, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered upon me and said: "Has it not been reported to me that you pray the night and fast the day?" I said: Yes. He said: "Do not do so. Pray and sleep, fast and break your fast, for your body has a right over you, your eye has a right over you, your visitor has a right over you, and your wife has a right over you." The wording mentioned is from the saying of Salman to Abu al-Darda, may Allah be pleased with them both, narrated by al-Bukhari (1968) from the hadith of Abu Juhayfa al-Suwa'i.], do not say, "I pray the night and fast the day as long as I live." This is wrong. "Indeed your Lord has a right over you" by worshipping Him, but "your self has a right over you" by giving it rest. So the correct position is this.

﴿And do not forget your share of this world﴾.

* Student: Shaykh.

* The Shaykh: Yes.

* Student: This, (...)?

* The Shaykh: We do not know whether this advice came before, while Pharaoh was still existing, or after. Allah knows best.

* Student: But the fact that (...)?

* The Shaykh: Yes, there is nothing preventing that this man disbelieved and joined Pharaoh, so he obtained great wealth. There is no obstacle.

He said: (﴿And be good﴾ to people through charity, ﴿as Allah has been good to you﴾).

Here the author restricted the goodness to charity, saying: (be good to people in charity). But the correct view is that the intended meaning is more general: be good in the worship of Allah and in dealing with the servants of Allah.

﴿And be good as Allah has been good to you﴾ [al-Qasas 77]. Is the kaf here for comparison or for causation?

* Student: For causation.
